introduction: “I am, I am, I am, the promised One!” The Báb’s declaration stands near the head of these passages, and the rest say who he understood himself to be and how Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá spoke of him: the Gate, the promised Qá’im, the Primal Point from which all things proceed, and at the same time the Herald of one greater, who wrote his own Book so that it would give way. A hundred of the guide’s 109 quotations are given here. Beside them stand a hundred voices from elsewhere, most of them from the Gospels and the Qur’an, because the readings constantly call on both: John the Baptist and the one whose shoe he would not unloose, the voice from the burning tree, the challenge to produce the like of a scripture, Simeon in the temple. About one in six asks something harder and ends in a question: the warning against false Christs, the test of a prophet in Deuteronomy, apostles who refused to be called gods, the curse on adding to a book, the commandment against images.
questions: The Báb is called both a sun in his own right and the herald of another. John’s Gospel says of the Baptist that he “was not that Light”. Why do the readings refuse to choose between the two descriptions?
“I am the promised One.” Jesus warned against those who would say, “Lo, here is Christ.” What tests do Deuteronomy, the Gospels and these readings offer for telling one claim from another?

The Tree of the Bayán speaks as God; Paul and Barnabas tore their clothes when called gods; Muḥammad was told to say he was a mortal messenger. How do the readings relate the voice to the one who speaks?

The Báb wrote that all the Bayán could not stand against one word of the One to come. Revelation ends with a curse on any who add to it. What does it say about a religion that its founder expects to be superseded?
A believer missed the Báb because he was not wearing the turban he expected. What outward signs do people look for today, and what did Samuel learn about them?

Recognition is said to bring all good and its absence fire, and yet ‘Abdu’l-Bahá notes how unreliable the histories are. How responsible is a person for recognizing someone of whom they have heard only confused reports?

outside.why: “Diverse tales are on the tongues … of men”, none as trustworthy as it should be; so ‘Abdu’l-Bahá sets down a sober account. Luke begins his Gospel for the same reason: that thou mightest know the certainty.
Some have written of the Báb “in extreme censure and condemnation”. The first Roman historian to mention the Christians did the same while describing how they were killed.

A new religion’s history is first written by its enemies and its partisans. Mill called it a pleasant falsehood that truth always triumphs over persecution. What does it take for a fair account to be written at all?
A believer looked for the green turban and did not know the Báb without it. Samuel, sent to choose a king: man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart.
He looked for a sign of dress. Jesus: judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.
“The Primal Point is verily the Truth from thy Lord; let not the deeds of men veil thee.” Paul: what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect?
One who had doubts brought them and “received the answer directly”. Thomas was answered so, and told: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.
Bahá’u’lláh calls the doubter “most unfair”. Tennyson: there lives more faith in honest doubt, believe me, than in half the creeds. When is doubt unfair, and when is it honest?
“I am, I am, I am, the promised One!” Jesus to the woman who said Messiah would come: I that speak unto thee am he.
“The One whose name you have for a thousand years invoked.” Simeon, who had waited all his life, in the temple: mine eyes have seen thy salvation.

The Báb declares himself the One awaited. Jesus had warned: if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Christ, believe it not. How is a hearer to tell the promised one from the false ones the same scripture foretells?
“I am the Gate of Knowledge.” Jesus: I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved.
Gate, then Qá’im, then Primal Point: the claim unfolded by degrees. Deuteronomy gives Israel a test for anyone who speaks in God’s name. What tests do the readings themselves propose?
The Báb is identified as the promised Qá’im, the twelfth Imám awaited. Jews awaited Elijah on the strength of this verse.

He is “the Morn of Truth” and “the Harbinger of the Most Great Light”. Zacharias over his infant son: thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways; the dayspring from on high hath visited us.

The Báb is called both a sun in his own right and a harbinger. John’s Gospel is careful to deny the first of the Baptist: he was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light. Why do the readings insist on both?
“The Herald of the Ancient Beauty.” Malachi: behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me.
‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls the Báb and Bahá’u’lláh two peerless Stars and himself their “weak, mortal servant”. Paul on the mind to be in a believer: took upon him the form of a servant.
‘Abdu’l-Bahá corrects a writer who had praised him too highly; his station is servitude. Milton’s Satan: better to reign in Hell, than serve in Heaven. What does each understand by greatness?
He is “the Primal Will … while all things are created by His bidding”. Wisdom in Proverbs: the Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.
“I am the Primal Point from which have been generated all created things.” John: in the beginning was the Word; all things were made by him.
Recognition brings “all good”; failure, “infernal fire”. Mark’s Gospel ends the same way: he that believeth not shall be damned. How do such warnings sit beside “no compulsion in religion”?
“God sent me forth after twenty-four years of my life.” Jeremiah objected that he was a child, and was told: say not, I am a child.
He was raised among those who do not speak Arabic, and yet revealed verses. The Qur’an’s own challenge: though mankind and the jinn should assemble, they could not produce the like.
An unschooled young man with a Book. The same was said of Jesus: how knoweth this man letters, having never learned?
“That which God revealed in twenty-three years is now revealed in four days.” The Psalm: my tongue is the pen of a ready writer.
“All the people clung to their religious leaders … and turned not” to him. John: he came unto his own, and his own received him not.
The servants followed their divines. The Pharisees’ argument against Jesus: have any of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed on him?
The Báb’s first book is a commentary on the story of Joseph. The dream with which that story begins.
“God offered Our authority to the heavens, earth and mountains; they refused to bear it.” The Báb is echoing this verse of the Qur’an.
“Thou hast brought all things into being through me.” Paul of Christ: by him were all things created, and by him all things consist.
“I made Myself known on the Day of Resurrection through the Point of the Bayán.” Jesus: I am the resurrection, and the life.
The Day of Resurrection is the day of the new Manifestation. Paul rested everything on a rising from the dead in history. What is kept, and what is changed, in the Báb’s use of the word?
“God testifieth that there is none other God but Him.” The form is the Qur’an’s.
“There is none other God but Him.” Israel’s oldest confession: the Lord our God is one Lord.
“The Primal Point was not as any one among you.” The officers sent to arrest Jesus: never man spake like this man.
The Tree of the Bayán spoke: “I am God.” The Qur’an tells of such a voice from a tree, to Moses.
A fire kindled, and a voice out of it. The scene in Exodus.

The Herald declares: “I, verily, am God.” Paul and Barnabas, hailed as gods, tore their clothes: we also are men of like passions with you. How do the readings distinguish the voice from the man through whom it speaks?
He speaks as God in every state. Muḥammad was told to say: am I aught save a mortal messenger? Do the two statements describe different things, or the same thing from two sides?
A single Point, containing all meanings, “then … became detailed, multiplied, branched out”. The Tao Te Ching: the One produced Two; Two produced Three; Three produced all things.
All realities gathered in a Point. Dante, shown a point of light in the highest heaven, is told: from that point dependent is the heaven and nature all.
From the Point came “books which none can reckon”. John ends his Gospel: the world itself could not contain the books that should be written.
Everything in the Qur’an is said to lie in its first chapter, and that in its first phrase, and that in a point. The chapter.
The whole in the smallest part. Blake: to see a world in a grain of sand, and eternity in an hour.
Through him “the point of creation hath been made to revolve”, and to him all returns. Plotinus on the One: it has overflowed, and its exuberance has produced the new.
“Magnify Thou, O Lord my God, Him Who is the Primal Point.” The Qur’an’s command to bless the Prophet is the model for such prayers.
A prayer for the breaking of the fast, which blesses the Primal Point. Isaiah on the fast God has chosen.
“Our Sovereign, our King, our Lord, our Beloved.” Scripture praises its messengers and also notes what they were like: the man Moses was very meek, above all the men upon the face of the earth.
“That Light of Divine Guidance … the Dawning-Place of the Luminary.” Isaiah: the people that walked in darkness have seen a great light.
“The Shining Star.” Peter: until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts.
“He is the most perfect Balance amongst nations.” The writing on Belshazzar’s wall: thou art weighed in the balances.
“Hearken to God’s call” from the direction of the Prison. Paul and Silas sang in theirs, and the prisoners heard them.
The Primal Point “drew aside the veil”. Paul: now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face.
The Primal Point “in His latter Manifestation” speaks again. Jesus of John the Baptist: if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.
“Do ye deny … Him Who created you from dust, then from a drop of fluid?” The question is the Qur’an’s.
“The Point Himself is resigned to the Will of Him Whom God shall make manifest.” John the Baptist: he must increase, but I must decrease.
The Báb’s “ultimate hope” was to be mentioned by the One to come. The Baptist: whose shoe’s latchet I am not worthy to unloose.
“All exist that they might be mentioned but once in the holy court.” Jesus: rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.
“He shall not be known through My allusions, nor through what hath been revealed in the Bayán.” God to Moses: by my name JEHOVAH was I not known to them.
He cannot be known through any allusion. The Tao Te Ching: the name that can be named is not the enduring and unchanging name.
All the Bayán “could not resist even one of His words”. Jesus said of his own: heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away. What kind of scripture is written to be superseded?
The Báb left his own Book open to whatever the next Revealer would say. Revelation closes with a curse on any who add to it. Which attitude to a sacred text is the more usual, and why?
Do not “pause at the time of His manifestation for anything”. The first disciples: they straightway left their nets, and followed him.
No pausing. Jesus: no man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.
“Creation has ranks”: a stone cannot become a ruby. Paul: one star differeth from another star in glory.

Not all can attain the station of the Prophets. Moses, told that others were prophesying in the camp: would God that all the Lord’s people were prophets. Is the difference of rank a limit on what God gives, or on what we can bear?
“Beware lest ye … cling to what ye possess from the tidings of the ancients.” Jesus: no man having drunk old wine straightway desireth new: for he saith, The old is better.
The Báb completed the Bayán with the remembrance of the One to come. Paul on the law of Moses: our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ.
“The Primal Point desired from the Bayán naught save My Self.” Jesus: search the scriptures; they are they which testify of me.
“Read ye the Bayán, that ye may know him.” Jesus to those who honoured Moses: had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me.
“‘Alí wept in His days until He sacrificed His life.” Jeremiah: oh that mine eyes were a fountain of tears.
He took a covenant from his people about the One to come. Jesus, weeping over Jerusalem: thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.
“I am indeed the Youth heralded by the Primal Point.” Jesus at Nazareth closed the book of Isaiah and said: this day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.
The Báb named a year: “in the year Nine ye shall be blessed”. Jesus said of the day and hour that no man knows, not even the Son. What is the use, and the risk, of a date in prophecy?
“The Primal Point … was the Herald of this Most Great Manifestation.” The Baptist of himself: I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness.
“Whoso hath attained unto but one word from Him — this is better for him than all that was revealed in the Bayán.” Paul: I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ.
“The All-Merciful hath come! He, verily, is the Promised One.” Haggai: the desire of all nations shall come.
He was “the morning star heralding the daybreak”. Malachi: unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise.
The Báb: “The Hour has come and the moon has been cleft asunder.” The words are the opening of this chapter of the Qur’an.
Elijah the prophet is read as ‘Alí-Muḥammad: a return in name and station. Hebrews: it is appointed unto men once to die. In what sense, then, do the readings speak of return?
“I desire only to be killed in Thy path.” Paul: to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
“This is He for Whose sake the Primal Point sacrificed Himself.” Jesus: greater love hath no man than this.
“Him Who was suspended in the air and sacrificed Himself.” Jesus of his own death: I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me.
He died that this might be manifested. Tertullian to Rome’s governors: the oftener we are mown down by you, the more in number we grow; the blood of Christians is seed.
He exposed “his sacred breast to a thousand bullets of tyranny”. Isaiah’s servant: he was wounded for our transgressions.
He laid down his life and “guided His lovers to self-sacrifice”. Jesus: except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone.
“We must follow His heavenly example.” Peter: Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps.
“We have chosen Quddús as Our companion.” The Bible’s great companionship: the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David.
“But for My incarceration in … the fortress of Chihríq.” Lovelace in prison: stone walls do not a prison make.
On the road to Máh-Kú, “outwardly veiled from all”. Paul: my bonds have fallen out rather unto the furtherance of the gospel.
“Spiritual Relationship is the true Family-hood of God’s children.” Jesus: whosoever shall do the will of my Father, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.
“The Báb had many relatives”, and wished above all that his mother should believe. John: neither did his brethren believe in him.
The Báb “would sometimes partake of frankincense and rock candy”. Frankincense is in the Gospel’s first scene of homage.
A small human detail is preserved of what he ate. The Gospels keep such details too, and the comment they drew: behold a gluttonous man, and a winebibber. Why do followers treasure them?

Portraits of Bahá’u’lláh and the Báb are kept and reverenced. The second commandment: thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness. How have the religions lived with likenesses of those they revere?
An elegy was composed for the Báb. English has a great one for a young man lost before his time, which turns into a lament for a neglected flock.
Shíráz has “become the dawning-place of the Morn of Oneness”. Micah of another small city: thou, Bethlehem, though thou be little, out of thee shall he come forth.
“That region was the homeland of the Great Announcer.” Nathanael on another homeland: can there any good thing come out of Nazareth? Come and see.
These servants “have believed in Thy unity and in Thy divine Word — the Primal Point”. Paul’s summary of a community’s faith: one Lord, one faith, one baptism.

luke-prophet-of-the-highest.text: And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways; To give knowledge of salvation unto his people by the remission of their sins, Through the tender mercy of our God; whereby the dayspring from on high hath visited us, To give light to them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace

malachi-my-messenger.text: Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in: behold, he shall come, saith the Lord of hosts

john-have-any-of-the-rulers.text: Then answered them the Pharisees, Are ye also deceived? Have any of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed on him

psalm-pen-of-a-ready-writer.text: My heart is inditing a good matter: I speak of the things which I have made touching the king: my tongue is the pen of a ready writer

john-i-am-the-door.text: I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture

matthew-left-their-nets.text: And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. And they straightway left their nets, and followed him

john-if-i-be-lifted-up.text: And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me

matthew-gold-frankincense-myrrh.text: And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense and myrrh

exodus-graven-image.text: Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth

john-out-of-nazareth.text: And Nathanael said unto him, Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth? Philip saith unto him, Come and see

john-judge-not-by-appearance.text: Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment

john-be-not-faithless.text: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing. And Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God. Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed

corinthians-star-differeth-from-star.text: There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars: for one star differeth from another star in glory

john-shoes-latchet.text: John answered them, saying, I baptize with water: but there standeth one among you, whom ye know not; He it is, who coming after me is preferred before me, whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose

proverbs-possessed-me-in-the-beginning.text: The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old. I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was

luke-names-written-in-heaven.text: Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven

romans-shall-their-unbelief.text: For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect

mark-believeth-not.text: He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned

philippians-form-of-a-servant.text: Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross

quran-verily-i-am-allah.text: Lo! I, even I, am Allah, There is no Allah save Me. So serve Me and establish worship for My remembrance.

quran-allah-is-witness.text: Allah (Himself) is Witness that there is no Allah save Him. And the angels and the men of learning (too are witness). Maintaining His creation in justice, there is no Allah save Him the Almighty, the Wise.

quran-created-thee-of-dust.text: His comrade, when he (thus) spake with him, exclaimed: Disbelievest thou in Him Who created thee of dust, then of a drop (of seed), and then fashioned thee a man?

dante-from-that-point.text: From that point / Dependent is the heaven and nature all
dante-from-that-point.author: Dante Alighieri
